1→# cmux iOS
     2→
     3→SwiftUI iOS/iPadOS shell for the CMUXMobileCore production path.
     4→
     5→Current phase:
     6→
     7→- Stack Auth sign-in gate with Apple, Google, email code, and a debug-only `42` shortcut
     8→- QR/manual pairing surface
     9→- CMUXMobileCore pairing payload and attach-ticket decoding
    10→- injectable `CmxByteTransportFactory` runtime hook
    11→- isolated preview host data when no concrete transport is installed
    12→- workspace list, workspace detail, terminal dropdown, and input bar
    13→
    14→No Rust, Iroh, or Zig dependency is linked into this shell. Concrete route implementations should enter through `CMUXMobileRuntime`.
    15→
    16→Build and reload the simulator:
    17→
    18→```bash
    19→ios/scripts/reload.sh --tag iossh
    20→```
    21→
    22→Run package tests:
    23→
    24→```bash
    25→swift test --package-path ios/cmuxPackage
    26→```
    27→
    28→## Build compatibility and production-auth DEV builds
    29→
    30→A DEV iOS build connects only to the Mac DEV build with the same tag. BETA,
    31→INTERNAL, and App Store iOS builds connect only to Stable or Nightly Mac builds.
    32→Account environment does not change that compatibility boundary.
    33→
    34→Use `--prod-auth` only when a tagged DEV build needs to test production account,
    35→registry, or API behavior:
    36→
    37→```bash
    38→ios/scripts/reload.sh --tag my-tag --device-only --prod-auth
    39→```
    40→
    41→What `--prod-auth` does:
    42→
    43→- Bakes `CMUXAuthEnvironment=production` into the app's Info.plist (via the
    44→  `CMUX_IOS_AUTH_ENV` build setting), so the build signs in against the
    45→  production Stack project and uses `https://cmux.com` for the device
    46→  registry/API and the magic-link callback.
    47→- Makes the presence worker follow the auth channel: the app resolves the
    48→  production presence instance (see `PresenceClient.productionServiceURL`) so
    49→  compatible Macs appear in Computers. The worker URLs live only in Swift;
    50→  the script bakes no copy, and an explicit `CMUX_PRESENCE_BASE_URL` still
    51→  wins.
    52→- Skips the dogfood auto sign-in/auto-pair (those credentials belong to the
    53→  development Stack project). Sign in in-app with the same account as your
    54→  matching tagged DEV Mac.
    55→- On first launch after switching auth environments on the same install, the
    56→  app clears the previous environment's session/caches (tokens and user ids
    57→  are per-Stack-project), so you start signed out instead of restoring a
    58→  stale identity.
    59→
    60→Every installed iOS bundle registers one URL scheme derived from its complete
    61→bundle identifier, for example `cmux-ios-dev.cmux.app.beta://…` or
    62→`cmux-ios-dev.cmux.ios.my-tag://…`. No two cmux builds register the same system
    63→route. The authenticated Mac status supplies the exact instance tag, which the
    64→app validates before it saves or adopts the connection.
    65→
    66→Without the flag, the same override is available by bundling a
    67→`LocalConfig.plist` with an `AuthEnvironment` string of `production` (see
    68→`MobileAuthComposition`); a `LocalConfig.plist` entry wins over the baked
    69→Info.plist value.
    70→
    71→## TestFlight beta (cloud lane)
    72→
    73→`ios/scripts/cloud-testflight.sh` is the turnkey lane for cutting a TestFlight
    74→beta. It builds the heavy GhosttyKit + Swift Release compile on a leased fleet
    75→Mac (same maclease pool as the device cloud reload, m1ultra excluded), so the
    76→build stays off this Mac's CPU. The fleet produces an UNSIGNED Release archive
    77→for the beta bundle id `dev.cmux.app.beta` (no signing material ever lands on
    78→the shared Macs), downloads it locally, then hands it to
    79→`ios/scripts/upload-testflight.sh --archive-path`, which does the local export,
    80→re-sign with the Apple Distribution cert (re-adding `aps-environment=production`),
    81→strict codesign verification, and TestFlight upload.
    82→
    83→```bash
    84→# Dry run: build + export + re-sign + verify aps-environment=production, NO upload
    85→ios/scripts/cloud-testflight.sh --no-upload
    86→
    87→# Full lane: build on the fleet and upload to TestFlight (internal "cmux beta" group)
    88→ios/scripts/cloud-testflight.sh
    89→
    90→# Also make the build eligible for external testers
    91→ios/scripts/cloud-testflight.sh --external
    92→```
    93→
    94→A standalone cmux clone with no cmuxterm-hq checkout transparently falls back to
    95→a LOCAL Release archive (`--local` forces it), then takes the same export path.
    96→
    97→Internal testers (the `cmux beta` group) get every uploaded build instantly with
    98→no review. An `--external` build is different: the FIRST external build of a new
    99→`MARKETING_VERSION` must pass a one-time Apple Beta App Review (~24h) before any
   100→external tester can install it. Subsequent external builds of the same version
   101→ship without re-review. External cuts reuse
   102→`CMUX_IOS_BETA_MARKETING_VERSION` from `ios/Config/Shared.xcconfig`; bump it
   103→only when you want a fresh Beta App Review cycle. The upload path assigns the
   104→processed build to both the Founder's Edition and Pro external beta groups. It
   105→uses `CMUX_TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP_ID` /
   106→`CMUX_TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP_NAME` for the primary group and
   107→`CMUX_TESTFLIGHT_PRO_GROUP_ID` for Pro. GitHub Actions maps the repository
   108→variables `IOS_TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP_ID`,
   109→`IOS_TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP_NAME`, and `IOS_TESTFLIGHT_PRO_GROUP_ID` to those
   110→script inputs. When Apple reports the build as `READY_FOR_BETA_SUBMISSION`, the
   111→same lane also creates the beta app review submission automatically so a new
   112→`MARKETING_VERSION` is not left stuck at "Ready to Submit".
   113→
   114→If CI is moved back from a pending higher version to the last approved version,
   115→external testers are unblocked because they could not install the pending build.
   116→Internal testers who already installed that higher internal-only build will not
   117→see lower-version builds as updates in TestFlight. They need a one-time app
   118→reinstall, or operators need to cut an internal-only build on the higher version.
   119→
   120→## TestFlight GitHub Actions signing
   121→
   122→`.github/workflows/ios-testflight.yml` uses manual export signing because Xcode's
   123→automatic App Store Connect export has produced IPAs whose signed app
   124→entitlements omit `aps-environment=production`. That upload is intentionally
   125→blocked because TestFlight push would silently fail. Scheduled `main` uploads
   126→ship only to the internal TestFlight group. A manual run with
   127→`marketing_version_override` switches to the external beta bundle, installs its
   128→provisioning profile, and assigns the processed build to both the Founder's
   129→Edition and Pro groups. That external override reuses an already approved
   130→marketing version and auto-submits the first build when Apple reports that Beta
   131→App Review is required.
   132→
   133→Required GitHub secrets:
   134→
   135→- `ASC_API_KEY_ID`
   136→- `ASC_API_ISSUER_ID`
   137→- `ASC_API_KEY_P8_BASE64`
   138→- `IOS_DISTRIBUTION_CERTIFICATE_BASE64` (base64-encoded `.p12` for an Apple Distribution certificate on team `7WLXT3NR37`)
   139→- `IOS_DISTRIBUTION_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`
   140→- `IOS_BETA_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64` (base64-encoded App Store profile for `dev.cmux.app.beta`, with `aps-environment=production`)
   141→
   142→## App Store production lane
   143→
   144→The production App Store lane is separate from the TestFlight beta lane. It uses
   145→the same archive/export/re-sign verification path, but switches the submitted
   146→identity to the App Store bundle id and stops before App Review submission unless
   147→the operator explicitly confirms submission in CI.
   148→
   149→```bash
   150→# Build, export, re-sign, verify, and upload the production App Store build
   151→ios/scripts/upload-app-store.sh
   152→
   153→# Dry run: export + re-sign + verify aps-environment=production, no upload
   154→ios/scripts/upload-app-store.sh --export-only
   155→
   156→# Run the read-only ASC readiness package after upload
   157→ios/scripts/validate-app-store-release.sh --app "$ASC_APP_ID" --build-number "$CF_BUNDLE_VERSION" --wait-build --strict
   158→```
   159→
   160→Defaults:
   161→
   162→- Bundle ID: `com.cmux.app`
   163→- Marketing version: `CMUX_IOS_APPSTORE_MARKETING_VERSION` in `ios/Config/Shared.xcconfig`
   164→- Display name: `cmux`
   165→- Provisioning profile: `cmux App Store Distribution`
   166→- Entitlements: `Config/cmux-release.entitlements`
   167→
   168→The review package lives in `ios/AppStoreReview/`:
   169→
   170→- `review-notes.md` is the pasteable App Store Connect Review Information notes source.
   171→- `metadata-screenshots-checklist.md` is the blocking checklist for metadata, screenshots, privacy, account deletion, and payment gating.
   172→
   173→`.github/workflows/ios-app-store.yml` is manual-only. It uploads a production
   174→build, waits for ASC processing, runs `ios/scripts/validate-app-store-release.sh`,
   175→and submits for review only when `submit_for_review` is set.
   176→
   177→Additional production workflow requirements:
   178→
   179→- Repository variable `IOS_APPSTORE_APP_ID`
   180→- Secret `IOS_APPSTORE_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64` (base64-encoded App Store profile for `com.cmux.app`, with `aps-environment=production`)
   181→

1→import CMUXMobileCore
     2→import CmuxMobileShell
     3→import CmuxMobileSupport
     4→import CmuxMobileTransport
     5→import Foundation
     6→import OSLog
     7→import SwiftUI
     8→import cmuxFeature
     9→#if DEBUG
    10→import CmuxIrohReleaseGateSupport
    11→#endif
    12→
    13→nonisolated private let cmuxAppConnectivityLog = Logger(
    14→    subsystem: Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier ?? "com.cmuxterm.app",
    15→    category: "connectivity"
    16→)
    17→
    18→@main
    19→struct cmuxApp: App {
    20→    @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor(CmuxAppDelegate.self) private var appDelegate
    21→    @Environment(\.scenePhase) private var scenePhase
    22→
    23→    /// The de-singletonized composition root: built once, injected down.
    24→    @MainActor
    25→    private static let root: AppCompositionRoot = {
    26→        let reachability = ReachabilityService()
    27→        let diagnosticLog = DiagnosticLog(
    28→            buildStamp: AppCompositionRoot.diagnosticBuildStamp,
    29→            role: .iosClient
    30→        )
    31→        let auth = MobileAuthComposition(
    32→            reachability: reachability,
    33→            diagnosticLog: diagnosticLog
    34→        )
    35→        // Per-tag isolation by default: this build pairs only with its own
    36→        // Mac tag plus the runtime grant set its anchor Mac advertises
    37→        // (`cmux mobile compatible-tags`), persisted across launches.
    38→        let buildCompatibilityPolicy = MobileMacBuildCompatibilityPolicy.current(
    39→            buildScope: MobileIOSBuildScope.current(),
    40→            additionalInstanceTags: MobileMacTagAllowlist.persisted()
    41→        )
    42→        let iroh = MobileIrohRuntimeComposition(
    43→            apiBaseURL: auth.config.apiBaseURL,
    44→            reachability: reachability,
    45→            discoveryCompatibilityPolicy: buildCompatibilityPolicy,
    46→            appNamespace: auth.appNamespace,
    47→            keychainAccessGroup: auth.keychainAccessGroup,
    48→            diagnosticLog: diagnosticLog
    49→        )
    50→        let connectivityInvalidationServiceURL = PresenceClient
    51→            .resolvedServiceBaseURL(
    52→                isDevelopmentAuthChannel: auth.authEnvironment == .development
    53→            )
    54→        let connectivityInvalidationBaseURL = connectivityInvalidationServiceURL
    55→            .flatMap { URL(string: $0) }
    56→        if connectivityInvalidationBaseURL == nil {
    57→            cmuxAppConnectivityLog.error(
    58→                "Connectivity invalidation disabled: presence service URL unavailable"
    59→            )
    60→        }
    61→        // Exactly one iroh runtime owns the app's broker binding slot: the
    62→        // irx rebuild when its DEBUG flag is on, the legacy composition
    63→        // otherwise. The unconfigured one stays dormant.
    64→        let irxEnabled = MobileIrxRuntimeComposition.isEnabled
    65→        let irx = MobileIrxRuntimeComposition(
    66→            apiBaseURL: auth.config.apiBaseURL,
    67→            appNamespace: auth.appNamespace,
    68→            keychainAccessGroup: auth.keychainAccessGroup
    69→        )
    70→        if irxEnabled {
    71→            let coordinator = auth.coordinator
    72→            Task {
    73→                await irx.configure(
    74→                    auth: coordinator,
    75→                    legacy: iroh,
    76→                    controlPlaneBaseURL: connectivityInvalidationBaseURL
    77→                )
    78→            }
    79→        } else {
    80→            iroh.configure(
    81→                auth: auth.coordinator,
    82→                connectivityInvalidationBaseURL: connectivityInvalidationBaseURL
    83→            )
    84→        }
    85→
    86→        // `debugLoopback` (127.0.0.1) backs the UI-test mock Mac. Enable it on
    87→        // the simulator and on DEBUG device builds so on-device XCUITests can
    88→        // attach to an in-runner mock host; release device builds keep only
    89→        // real transports. Force-relay mode (soak rigs) registers NO fallback
    90→        // kinds so even a simulator exercises the real relay path.
    91→        let forceRelay = MobileIrxRuntimeComposition.forceRelayOnly
    92→        #if targetEnvironment(simulator) || DEBUG
    93→        let supportedKinds: [CmxAttachTransportKind] =
    94→            forceRelay ? [] : [.debugLoopback, .tailscale]
    95→        #else
    96→        let supportedKinds: [CmxAttachTransportKind] = forceRelay ? [] : [.tailscale]
    97→        #endif
    98→        let networkFactory = CmxNetworkByteTransportFactory(supportedKinds: supportedKinds)
    99→        let fallbackRegistrations = supportedKinds.map { kind in
   100→            CmxRouteTransportFactoryRegistration(kind: kind, factory: networkFactory)
   101→        }
   102→        let registrations = [
   103→            CmxRouteTransportFactoryRegistration(
   104→                kind: .iroh,
   105→                factory: irxEnabled ? irx.transportFactory : iroh.transportFactory
   106→            ),
   107→        ] + fallbackRegistrations
   108→        let transportFactory: CmxRouteTransportFactory
   109→        do {
   110→            transportFactory = try CmxRouteTransportFactory(registrations)
   111→        } catch {
   112→            preconditionFailure("Invalid mobile transport registrations: \(error)")
   113→        }
   114→
   115→        let runtime = CMUXMobileRuntime(
   116→            transportFactory: transportFactory,
   117→            stackAccessTokenProvider: CMUXMobileRuntime.stackAccessTokenProvider(from: auth.coordinator),
   118→            stackAccessTokenForStatusProvider: CMUXMobileRuntime.stackAccessTokenForStatusProvider(from: auth.coordinator),
   119→            stackAccessTokenForceRefresher: CMUXMobileRuntime.stackAccessTokenForceRefresher(from: auth.coordinator),
   120→            independentEventByteStreamProvider: { request in
   121→                irxEnabled
   122→                    ? try await irx.serverEventByteStream(for: request)
   123→                    : try await iroh.serverEventByteStream(for: request)
   124→            },
   125→            terminalLaneProvider: { request, surfaceID, cursor in
   126→                guard let surfaceUUID = UUID(uuidString: surfaceID) else {
   127→                    throw MobileIrohTerminalLaneError.invalidSurfaceID
   128→                }
   129→                return irxEnabled
   130→                    ? try await irx.openTerminalLane(

   362→    /// The most recent scene phase, so a `.active` transition is classified as a
   363→    /// cold first foreground vs. a warm resume.
   364→    private var hasForegrounded = false
   365→    /// When the current session started, for the best-effort `ios_session_ended`
   366→    /// duration emitted on background.
   367→    private var currentSessionStartedAt: Date?
   368→    /// The id of the session currently in progress, echoed onto `ios_session_ended`.

   370→
   371→    /// Drives the app-lifecycle + sessionization analytics on scene-phase changes.
   372→    ///
   373→    /// On `.active`: resolves the session (cold start or 30-min-gap resume) via
   374→    /// the injected ``CmuxMobileAnalytics/AnalyticsSessionizer`` and persisted
   375→    /// ``CmuxMobileAnalytics/AnalyticsSessionStore``, emitting `ios_session_started`
   376→    /// only when a new session begins, plus an `ios_app_foregrounded` heartbeat.
   377→    /// On `.background`: records the timestamp for the next gap calculation,
   378→    /// emits `ios_app_backgrounded`, and force-flushes queued events before
   379→    /// suspension.
   380→    func handleScenePhase(_ phase: ScenePhase) {
   381→        let emitter = analytics.emitter
   382→        switch phase {
   383→        case .active:
   384→            diagnosticLog.recordAppEvent(.appForegrounded)
   385→            connectionMethodStore.recordConfiguredMethodDiagnostic()
   386→            let isFullForegroundReturn = iroh.didBecomeActive()
   387→            if let irx {
   388→                // Credential freshness re-check + engine warm-up: iOS
   389→                // suspension pauses the autopilot's sleep loop.
   390→                Task { await irx.didBecomeActive() }
   391→            }
   392→            // A notification-permission prompt is itself a transient inactive
   393→            // edge, so readiness still observes every active transition.
   394→            Task { await pushCoordinator.refreshReadiness() }
   395→            guard isFullForegroundReturn else { return }
   396→            featureFlags.refreshOnForeground()
   397→            let now = Date()
   398→            let decision = analytics.sessionizer.resolveForeground(
   399→                now: now,
   400→                lastBackgroundedAt: analytics.sessionStore.lastBackgroundedAt,
   401→                currentSessionID: analytics.sessionStore.currentSessionID
   402→            )
   403→            analytics.sessionStore.setCurrentSessionID(decision.sessionID)
   404→            let launchType = hasForegrounded ? "warm" : "cold"
   405→            currentSessionID = decision.sessionID.uuidString
   406→            if decision.startedNewSession {
   407→                currentSessionStartedAt = now
   408→                emitter.capture("ios_session_started", [
   409→                    "session_id": .string(decision.sessionID.uuidString),
   410→                    "launch_type": .string(launchType),
   411→                ])
   412→            }
   413→            var foregroundProps: [String: AnalyticsValue] = ["launch_type": .string(launchType)]
   414→            if let gap = decision.secondsSinceBackgrounded {
   415→                foregroundProps["seconds_since_backgrounded"] = .int(Int(gap))
   416→            }
   417→            emitter.capture("ios_app_foregrounded", foregroundProps)
   418→            hasForegrounded = true
   419→        case .inactive:
   420→            diagnosticLog.recordAppEvent(.appBecameInactive)
   421→            // The switcher opened; a swipe-kill from here may skip the
   422→            // background transition entirely, so snapshot diagnostics now.

     6→/// A mounted terminal view obtains the stream for its surface, feeds each

    14→/// This replaces the previous `(Data) -> Void` sink registry so output

## Comprehensive Summary: cmux iOS App Architecture & Features

Based on my thorough exploration of the cmux iOS codebase, here's a detailed breakdown of the app's functionality, architecture, and key features:

---

### **1. CORE FUNCTIONALITY & PURPOSE**

The cmux iOS app is a **remote terminal and computer management client** that allows users to interact with their Mac computers from their iPhone/iPad. It's part of the larger cmux ecosystem that provides multi-machine workspace orchestration. The app is a **SwiftUI iOS/iPadOS shell** built on top of the CMUXMobileCore framework, with NO Rust, Iroh, or Zig dependencies linked directly into the iOS app.

**Key Capabilities:**
- Remote terminal access to Mac workspaces
- Multi-computer management and switching
- Real-time workspace and terminal synchronization
- Push notifications from Mac hosts
- Browser panel streaming and interaction
- Simulator panel streaming for Mac simulators
- Task/todo status management
- File browser and artifact sharing

---

### **2. MAIN SCREENS & NAVIGATION**

The app follows a hierarchical navigation structure:

#### **Authentication & Pairing Flow:**
- **Sign-in Gate**: Stack Auth with Apple, Google, email codes (debug mode supports `42` shortcut)
- **QR/Manual Pairing**: Decode pairing payloads and attach tickets from Mac
- **Onboarding**: First-run introduction and connection setup

#### **Main Screens:**
1. **Workspace List** - Lists all workspaces from paired Mac(s), with device tree view
2. **Workspace Detail** - Shows terminal list, browser panels, simulator panels, and task composer
3. **Terminal View** - Interactive terminal with:
   - Text input with keyboard accessory
   - Terminal rendering (supports both raw bytes and optimized render-grid format)
   - Zoom controls
   - Recovery/stress testing features
4. **Browser Panel View** - Streaming browser windows with keyboard/mouse input
5. **Simulator Panel View** - macOS simulator output streaming with touch input
6. **Settings** - Display settings, connection methods, Tailscale configuration, Iroh settings
7. **Computers/Devices Screen** - Device management, Mac discovery, pairing, hidden computer management
8. **What's New** - Remote announcement display

#### **Modal Sheets:**
- Add Device (pairing flow)
- Workspace Changes summary
- Settings (display, connection, advanced)
- Diagnostics viewer
- File browser (for attachment selection)

---

### **3. ARCHITECTURE & KEY MODULES**

The iOS codebase is organized into **22 Swift Package Manager (SPM) packages** in `Packages/iOS/`:

#### **Core Packages:**

**CmuxMobileShell** (~200 files)
- Main facade: `MobileShellComposite` - The central state manager combining connection lifecycle, workspace/terminal lists, and terminal output pipeline
- Connection management: Mac discovery, pairing, connection attempts, automatic reconnection
- Workspace/terminal synchronization from the Mac
- Terminal replay and render-grid output handling
- Multi-Mac connection pooling (up to 5 live sessions)
- Browser and simulator stream lifecycle coordination

**CmuxMobileShellModel**
- Terminal output data models: `MobileTerminalOutputChunk`, `MobileTerminalRenderGridFrame`
- Viewport policies (natural height vs remote grid)
- Terminal draft storage
- Toast notifications
- State synchronization records

**CmuxMobileTerminal**
- `GhosttySurfaceView` - UIKit wrapper for Ghostty's libghostty rendering engine
- Text input handling: `TerminalInputTextView` with custom IME support
- Touch gestures and hardware keyboard input
- Terminal zoom controls and font preferences
- Artifact chip rendering for terminal-embedded artifacts
- Verified replay recovery mechanism for render-grid synchronization
- Bottom scroll stress testing for reliability

**CmuxMobileRPC**
- `MobileSyncRuntime` protocol - Runtime configuration interface
- `MobileCoreRPCSession` - RPC communication layer managing request/response lifecycle
- Protocol definitions for terminal lanes, artifact lanes, event subscriptions
- Request/response DTOs for workspace, terminal, browser, simulator operations
- Connection state management

**CmuxMobileShellUI**
- `CMUXMobileRootView` - Main SwiftUI root view
- `MobileRootPresentationState` - Modal sheet coordination
- Workspace list UI with drag-drop support
- Terminal selection and switching
- Settings and diagnostics UI
- Composer dock and task management

**CmuxMobileWorkspace**
- `MobileRootAuthGate` - Auth barrier before shell access
- `MobileOnboardingGate` - First-run onboarding flow
- Connection method UI (Auto-Connect vs Tailscale)
- Setup guidance states
- Terminal landscape camera edge handling

**CmuxMobileTransport**
- `CmxNetworkByteTransport` - Network.framework TCP transport wrapper
- Tailscale transport binding
- Reachability monitoring (`ReachabilityService`)
- Network error classification for user-friendly messages
- Supports both debug loopback (simulator) and Tailscale paths

**CmuxMobilePairedMac**
- `MobilePairedMacStoring` - Protocol for persisting paired Mac information
- Backup/restore of paired Mac state
- Mac alias and hide-computer management
- Mac version tracking and update hints
- Build compatibility policy enforcement

**CmuxMobileRPC**
- Low-level RPC client implementation
- Attach ticket creation and validation
- Token management and auth handling
- Transport connection pooling

**CmuxMobileBrowser**
- `BrowserSurfaceStore` - Browser panel state and lifecycle
- Browser frame/state event handling
- Dialog management
- URL resolution

**CmuxMobileSimulatorStream**
- Simulator panel rendering and interaction
- Frame streaming pipeline
- Touch point mapping

**CmuxMobileCamera**
- QR code scanning for pairing
- Frame capture and metadata parsing
- Camera authorization handling

**CmuxMobileAnalytics**
- PostHog-backed analytics and telemetry
- Session tracking (cold/warm launches)
- Event emission and batch flushing
- Consent management

**CmuxMobileDiagnostics**
- Structured diagnostic logging (privacy-safe)
- Diagnostic report generation and export
- App lifecycle diagnostics
- Connection incident tracking

**CmuxMobileCrashReporting**
- Sentry integration for crash reporting
- Consent-based crash data collection

**CmuxMobileSupport**
- Auth composition (`MobileAuthComposition`)
- Push notification coordination
- Display settings management
- Toast notifications

**CmuxAgentChatUI**
- Agent chat interface components
- Artifact viewer for code/markdown
- Chat prose parsing and rendering

---

### **4. HOW iOS COMMUNICATES WITH MAC**

#### **Connection Flow:**

1. **Pairing Phase:**
   - User scans QR code or enters manual code from Mac
   - iOS decodes `CMUXMobileCore.CmxAttachTicket` (compact binary format)
   - Ticket includes Mac instance info, route choices, authorization
   - iOS validates ticket against build compatibility policy

2. **Transport Layer:**
   - `CMUXMobileRuntime` owns the transport factory and route discovery
   - `CmxNetworkByteTransport` establishes TCP connection via Network.framework
   - Supports multiple transport types:
     - **Iroh** (primary): Encrypted, NAT-traversal capable peer-to-peer
     - **Tailscale**: Encrypted tunnel through Tailscale network
     - **Debug Loopback** (127.0.0.1): For simulator/testing
   - Connection attempts with configurable timeouts (15-30 seconds)
   - Automatic reconnection with exponential backoff

3. **RPC Protocol:**
   - Binary RPC protocol via `MobileCoreRPCSession`
   - Authenticated with Stack Auth tokens (plus attach tickets for pairing)
   - Structured request/response messages with tagged routing
   - Event-based updates for real-time synchronization

4. **Data Streams:**
   - **Terminal Output**: ASCII VT patches (render-grid optimized) or raw PTY bytes
     - Cold-attach replay on mount to catch up to current state
     - Verified replay ensures grid consistency
   - **Browser Frames**: High-frequency video stream of browser windows
   - **Simulator Frames**: macOS simulator display streaming
   - **Events**: Server-pushed events (workspace updates, notifications, etc.)
   - **Independent Lanes**: Dedicated transport lanes for terminal I/O, artifacts, simulators

5. **Session Management:**
   - Connection pooling: Keeps up to 5 Mac connections alive (1 focused + 4 warm)
   - Intelligent focus switching with session preservation
   - Automatic recovery on network changes
   - Per-request timeout enforcement (30 seconds default, 8 seconds for pairing)

#### **Data Sync Protocol:**
- `MobileStateSyncProtocol` for structured state mirroring
- Workspace list synchronization
- Terminal metadata and capabilities
- Notification feed delivery
- Caffeine (keep-awake) status
- Compatible Mac tags for multi-device access

---

### **5. KEY DATA MODELS**

```swift
// Workspaces & Terminals
MobileSyncWorkspaceListResponse    // Full workspace hierarchy
MobileTerminalRenderGridFrame      // Optimized terminal output
MobileTerminalOutputChunk          // Terminal data to render
MobileStateSyncRecords             // State deltas

// Browser/Simulator
MobileBrowserFrameEvent            // Video frame for browser
MobileSimulatorFrameEvent          // Video frame for simulator
MobileBrowserDialogQueue           // Dialog/prompt handling

// Connection & Auth
CmxAttachTicket                    // Pairing credential
CmxByteTransportRequest            // Transport request
MobileShellConnectionError         // Typed connection errors
MobilePairingFailure               // Pairing-specific errors

// Notifications
MobileNotificationFeedListItem     // Notification metadata
MobileTodoItem                     // Task/todo item

// Device Management
CmxMacAppInstanceIdentity          // Mac app identification
MobilePairedMacBackup              // Persisted Mac info
MobileDiscoveredIrohMac            // Discovery result
```

---

### **6. AUTHENTICATION & AUTHORIZATION**

- **Sign-in**: Stack Auth (backend service) with Google, Apple, or email
- **Token Management**: 
  - Access tokens from Stack Auth coordinator
  - Tokens cached and refreshed automatically
  - Force-refresh on 401 responses
- **Attach Tickets**: Compact binary format encoding Mac route/auth info
- **Build Compatibility**: 
  - DEV iOS builds pair only with same-tag DEV Mac
  - Beta/Release iOS builds pair only with Stable/Nightly Mac builds
  - Optional allowlist for cross-tag access via `compatible-tags` CLI
- **Diagnostics**: Privacy-safe structured logging (no credentials, no free-form text)

---

### **7. PUSH NOTIFICATIONS**

## Comprehensive Summary: cmux iOS App Architecture & Features

Based on my thorough exploration of the cmux iOS codebase, here's a detailed breakdown of the app's functionality, architecture, and key features:

---

### **1. CORE FUNCTIONALITY & PURPOSE**

The cmux iOS app is a **remote terminal and computer management client** that allows users to interact with their Mac computers from their iPhone/iPad. It's part of the larger cmux ecosystem that provides multi-machine workspace orchestration. The app is a **SwiftUI iOS/iPadOS shell** built on top of the CMUXMobileCore framework, with NO Rust, Iroh, or Zig dependencies linked directly into the iOS app.

**Key Capabilities:**
- Remote terminal access to Mac workspaces
- Multi-computer management and switching
- Real-time workspace and terminal synchronization
- Push notifications from Mac hosts
- Browser panel streaming and interaction
- Simulator panel streaming for Mac simulators
- Task/todo status management
- File browser and artifact sharing

---

### **2. MAIN SCREENS & NAVIGATION**

The app follows a hierarchical navigation structure:

#### **Authentication & Pairing Flow:**
- **Sign-in Gate**: Stack Auth with Apple, Google, email codes (debug mode supports `42` shortcut)
- **QR/Manual Pairing**: Decode pairing payloads and attach tickets from Mac
- **Onboarding**: First-run introduction and connection setup

#### **Main Screens:**
1. **Workspace List** - Lists all workspaces from paired Mac(s), with device tree view
2. **Workspace Detail** - Shows terminal list, browser panels, simulator panels, and task composer
3. **Terminal View** - Interactive terminal with:
   - Text input with keyboard accessory
   - Terminal rendering (supports both raw bytes and optimized render-grid format)
   - Zoom controls
   - Recovery/stress testing features
4. **Browser Panel View** - Streaming browser windows with keyboard/mouse input
5. **Simulator Panel View** - macOS simulator output streaming with touch input
6. **Settings** - Display settings, connection methods, Tailscale configuration, Iroh settings
7. **Computers/Devices Screen** - Device management, Mac discovery, pairing, hidden computer management
8. **What's New** - Remote announcement display

#### **Modal Sheets:**
- Add Device (pairing flow)
- Workspace Changes summary
- Settings (display, connection, advanced)
- Diagnostics viewer
- File browser (for attachment selection)

---

### **3. ARCHITECTURE & KEY MODULES**

The iOS codebase is organized into **22 Swift Package Manager (SPM) packages** in `Packages/iOS/`:

#### **Core Packages:**

**CmuxMobileShell** (~200 files)
- Main facade: `MobileShellComposite` - The central state manager combining connection lifecycle, workspace/terminal lists, and terminal output pipeline
- Connection management: Mac discovery, pairing, connection attempts, automatic reconnection
- Workspace/terminal synchronization from the Mac
- Terminal replay and render-grid output handling
- Multi-Mac connection pooling (up to 5 live sessions)
- Browser and simulator stream lifecycle coordination

**CmuxMobileShellModel**
- Terminal output data models: `MobileTerminalOutputChunk`, `MobileTerminalRenderGridFrame`
- Viewport policies (natural height vs remote grid)
- Terminal draft storage
- Toast notifications
- State synchronization records

**CmuxMobileTerminal**
- `GhosttySurfaceView` - UIKit wrapper for Ghostty's libghostty rendering engine
- Text input handling: `TerminalInputTextView` with custom IME support
- Touch gestures and hardware keyboard input
- Terminal zoom controls and font preferences
- Artifact chip rendering for terminal-embedded artifacts
- Verified replay recovery mechanism for render-grid synchronization
- Bottom scroll stress testing for reliability

**CmuxMobileRPC**
- `MobileSyncRuntime` protocol - Runtime configuration interface
- `MobileCoreRPCSession` - RPC communication layer managing request/response lifecycle
- Protocol definitions for terminal lanes, artifact lanes, event subscriptions
- Request/response DTOs for workspace, terminal, browser, simulator operations
- Connection state management

**CmuxMobileShellUI**
- `CMUXMobileRootView` - Main SwiftUI root view
- `MobileRootPresentationState` - Modal sheet coordination
- Workspace list UI with drag-drop support
- Terminal selection and switching
- Settings and diagnostics UI
- Composer dock and task management

**CmuxMobileWorkspace**
- `MobileRootAuthGate` - Auth barrier before shell access
- `MobileOnboardingGate` - First-run onboarding flow
- Connection method UI (Auto-Connect vs Tailscale)
- Setup guidance states
- Terminal landscape camera edge handling

**CmuxMobileTransport**
- `CmxNetworkByteTransport` - Network.framework TCP transport wrapper
- Tailscale transport binding
- Reachability monitoring (`ReachabilityService`)
- Network error classification for user-friendly messages
- Supports both debug loopback (simulator) and Tailscale paths

**CmuxMobilePairedMac**
- `MobilePairedMacStoring` - Protocol for persisting paired Mac information
- Backup/restore of paired Mac state
- Mac alias and hide-computer management
- Mac version tracking and update hints
- Build compatibility policy enforcement

**CmuxMobileRPC**
- Low-level RPC client implementation
- Attach ticket creation and validation
- Token management and auth handling
- Transport connection pooling

**CmuxMobileBrowser**
- `BrowserSurfaceStore` - Browser panel state and lifecycle
- Browser frame/state event handling
- Dialog management
- URL resolution

**CmuxMobileSimulatorStream**
- Simulator panel rendering and interaction
- Frame streaming pipeline
- Touch point mapping

**CmuxMobileCamera**
- QR code scanning for pairing
- Frame capture and metadata parsing
- Camera authorization handling

**CmuxMobileAnalytics**
- PostHog-backed analytics and telemetry
- Session tracking (cold/warm launches)
- Event emission and batch flushing
- Consent management

**CmuxMobileDiagnostics**
- Structured diagnostic logging (privacy-safe)
- Diagnostic report generation and export
- App lifecycle diagnostics
- Connection incident tracking

**CmuxMobileCrashReporting**
- Sentry integration for crash reporting
- Consent-based crash data collection

**CmuxMobileSupport**
- Auth composition (`MobileAuthComposition`)
- Push notification coordination
- Display settings management
- Toast notifications

**CmuxAgentChatUI**
- Agent chat interface components
- Artifact viewer for code/markdown
- Chat prose parsing and rendering

---

### **4. HOW iOS COMMUNICATES WITH MAC**

#### **Connection Flow:**

1. **Pairing Phase:**
   - User scans QR code or enters manual code from Mac
   - iOS decodes `CMUXMobileCore.CmxAttachTicket` (compact binary format)
   - Ticket includes Mac instance info, route choices, authorization
   - iOS validates ticket against build compatibility policy

2. **Transport Layer:**
   - `CMUXMobileRuntime` owns the transport factory and route discovery
   - `CmxNetworkByteTransport` establishes TCP connection via Network.framework
   - Supports multiple transport types:
     - **Iroh** (primary): Encrypted, NAT-traversal capable peer-to-peer
     - **Tailscale**: Encrypted tunnel through Tailscale network
     - **Debug Loopback** (127.0.0.1): For simulator/testing
   - Connection attempts with configurable timeouts (15-30 seconds)
   - Automatic reconnection with exponential backoff

3. **RPC Protocol:**
   - Binary RPC protocol via `MobileCoreRPCSession`
   - Authenticated with Stack Auth tokens (plus attach tickets for pairing)
   - Structured request/response messages with tagged routing
   - Event-based updates for real-time synchronization

4. **Data Streams:**
   - **Terminal Output**: ASCII VT patches (render-grid optimized) or raw PTY bytes
     - Cold-attach replay on mount to catch up to current state
     - Verified replay ensures grid consistency
   - **Browser Frames**: High-frequency video stream of browser windows
   - **Simulator Frames**: macOS simulator display streaming
   - **Events**: Server-pushed events (workspace updates, notifications, etc.)
   - **Independent Lanes**: Dedicated transport lanes for terminal I/O, artifacts, simulators

5. **Session Management:**
   - Connection pooling: Keeps up to 5 Mac connections alive (1 focused + 4 warm)
   - Intelligent focus switching with session preservation
   - Automatic recovery on network changes
   - Per-request timeout enforcement (30 seconds default, 8 seconds for pairing)

#### **Data Sync Protocol:**
- `MobileStateSyncProtocol` for structured state mirroring
- Workspace list synchronization
- Terminal metadata and capabilities
- Notification feed delivery
- Caffeine (keep-awake) status
- Compatible Mac tags for multi-device access

---

### **5. KEY DATA MODELS**

```swift
// Workspaces & Terminals
MobileSyncWorkspaceListResponse    // Full workspace hierarchy
MobileTerminalRenderGridFrame      // Optimized terminal output
MobileTerminalOutputChunk          // Terminal data to render
MobileStateSyncRecords             // State deltas

// Browser/Simulator
MobileBrowserFrameEvent            // Video frame for browser
MobileSimulatorFrameEvent          // Video frame for simulator
MobileBrowserDialogQueue           // Dialog/prompt handling

// Connection & Auth
CmxAttachTicket                    // Pairing credential
CmxByteTransportRequest            // Transport request
MobileShellConnectionError         // Typed connection errors
MobilePairingFailure               // Pairing-specific errors

// Notifications
MobileNotificationFeedListItem     // Notification metadata
MobileTodoItem                     // Task/todo item

// Device Management
CmxMacAppInstanceIdentity          // Mac app identification
MobilePairedMacBackup              // Persisted Mac info
MobileDiscoveredIrohMac            // Discovery result
```

---

### **6. AUTHENTICATION & AUTHORIZATION**

- **Sign-in**: Stack Auth (backend service) with Google, Apple, or email
- **Token Management**: 
  - Access tokens from Stack Auth coordinator
  - Tokens cached and refreshed automatically
  - Force-refresh on 401 responses
- **Attach Tickets**: Compact binary format encoding Mac route/auth info
- **Build Compatibility**: 
  - DEV iOS builds pair only with same-tag DEV Mac
  - Beta/Release iOS builds pair only with Stable/Nightly Mac builds
  - Optional allowlist for cross-tag access via `compatible-tags` CLI
- **Diagnostics**: Privacy-safe structured logging (no credentials, no free-form text)

---

### **7. PUSH NOTIFICATIONS**

- **Registration**: Device registers for push tokens with cmux backend
- **Delivery**: APNS-based notifications from Mac → backend → iPhone
- **Handling**: Background task delivery, reply-relay for inline responses
- **Account-scoped**: Push token invalidated on sign-out

---

### **8. KEY FEATURES**

1. **Terminal Access**
   - Full PTY interaction with keyboard/mouse/gestures
   - Zoom controls
   - Scrollback history
   - Render-grid optimization (CPU-efficient rendering)

2. **Multi-Computer**
   - Discover nearby Macs via Iroh
   - Pair with QR code or manual entry
   - Hide/unhide computers
   - Auto-connect to previously paired Mac

3. **Browser Panels**
   - Stream and interact with browser windows opened on Mac
   - Full keyboard and mouse input support
   - Dialog handling (alerts, confirms, text inputs)

4. **Simulator Panels**
   - Stream macOS simulator display
   - Touch input mapping

5. **Notifications**
   - Real-time notification feed from Mac
   - Badge counts
   - Push notifications
   - Inline reply capability

6. **Settings**
   - Display preferences (text size, theme, etc.)
   - Connection method selection (Auto-Connect vs Tailscale)
   - Iroh relay/path preferences
   - Crash reporting consent

7. **Diagnostics**
   - Structured app and network logs
   - Export diagnostic reports
   - Connection state debugging

8. **Onboarding**
   - First-run setup flow
   - Tailscale verification
   - Auto-Connect migration (BETA → Release)

---

### **9. IMPLEMENTATION HIGHLIGHTS**

**Composition Root** (`AppCompositionRoot`):
- Builds entire dependency graph at app launch
- Injects: `CMUXMobileRuntime`, auth, push coordinator, analytics, feature flags
- Manages app lifecycle diagnostics
- Coordinates sign-out cleanup

**State Management**:
- `@Observable` architecture (Swift 5.9+)
- `MobileShellComposite` as the central store
- View-level `@State` for modal presentation
- No singletons (de-singletonized through DI)

- Dual output pipeline: raw bytes OR render-grid frames
- Verified replay to ensure grid consistency across network jitter
- Local pixel-level scrolling for smooth UX

- Network.framework for TCP
- Iroh for encrypted peer-to-peer (with relay fallback)
- Tailscale for VPN-based access
- Automatic retry with configurable timeouts

**Testing**:

### **10. BUILD & DEPLOYMENT**

   181→        self.maximumReceiveLength = maximumReceiveLength
   182→        self.connectTimeoutNanoseconds = max(1, connectTimeoutNanoseconds)
   183→        tailscaleBinding = nil

   186→    init(
   187→        request: CmxByteTransportRequest,
   188→        preparedTailscaleRoute: CmxPreparedTailscaleRoute,
   189→        tailscaleRouteAuthority: any CmxTailscaleRouteAuthorizing,

   192→    ) throws {

   197→            throw CmxNetworkByteTransportError.tailscaleAuthorizationUnavailable

   199→        guard let nwPort = NWEndpoint.Port(
   200→            rawValue: UInt16(exactly: preparedTailscaleRoute.proof.peerPort) ?? 0
   201→        ), nwPort != .any else {
   202→            throw CmxNetworkByteTransportError.invalidPort(preparedTailscaleRoute.proof.peerPort)
   203→        }
   204→
   205→        let tcpOptions = NWProtocolTCP.Options()
   206→        tcpOptions.noDelay = true
   207→        let parameters = NWParameters(tls: nil, tcp: tcpOptions)
   208→        parameters.requiredInterface = preparedTailscaleRoute.requiredInterface
   209→        connection = NWConnection(
   210→            host: preparedTailscaleRoute.proof.peerAddress.nwHost,
   211→            port: nwPort,
   212→            using: parameters
   213→        )
   214→        callbackQueue = DispatchQueue(
   215→            label: "dev.cmux.mobile.tailscale-network-byte-transport.\(UUID().uuidString)"
   216→        )
   217→        self.maximumReceiveLength = maximumReceiveLength
   218→        self.connectTimeoutNanoseconds = max(1, connectTimeoutNanoseconds)
   219→        tailscaleBinding = CmxTailscaleTransportBinding(
   220→            request: request,
   221→            preparedRoute: preparedTailscaleRoute,
   222→            authority: tailscaleRouteAuthority

   226→    /// Opens the connection, awaiting `ready` or failing on error/timeout.
   227→    /// - Throws: ``CmxNetworkByteTransportError`` or `CancellationError`.
   228→    public func connect() async throws {
   229→        try Task.checkCancellation()
   230→        let operationID = UUID()
   231→        try await withTaskCancellationHandler {
   232→            try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
   233→                startConnect(operationID: operationID, continuation: continuation)
   234→            }
   235→        } onCancel: {
   236→            Task { await self.cancelConnect(operationID: operationID) }
   237→        }
   238→    }

   240→    /// Receives the next chunk of bytes, or `nil` at end of stream.
   241→    /// - Returns: The next received `Data`, or `nil` once the peer closed.
   242→    /// - Throws: ``CmxNetworkByteTransportError`` or `CancellationError`.
   243→    public func receive() async throws -> Data? {
   244→        try Task.checkCancellation()
   245→        let operationID = UUID()
   246→        return try await withTaskCancellationHandler {
   247→            return try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
   248→                startReceive(operationID: operationID, continuation: continuation)
   249→            }
   250→        } onCancel: {
   251→            Task { await self.cancelReceive(operationID: operationID) }
   252→        }
   253→    }

   255→    /// Sends bytes over the connection. Empty data is a no-op.
   256→    /// - Parameter data: The bytes to write.
   257→    /// - Throws: ``CmxNetworkByteTransportError`` or `CancellationError`.
   258→    public func send(_ data: Data) async throws {
   259→        guard !data.isEmpty else {
   260→            return
   261→        }
   262→        try Task.checkCancellation()
   263→        let operationID = UUID()
   264→        try await withTaskCancellationHandler {
   265→            try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
   266→                Task {
   267→                    await self.startSend(
   268→                        data,
   269→                        operationID: operationID,
   270→                        continuation: continuation
   271→                    )
   272→                }
   273→            }
   274→        } onCancel: {
   275→            Task { await self.cancelSend(operationID: operationID) }
   276→        }
   277→    }

   279→    /// Cancels the connection and completes any in-flight operations.
   280→    ///
   281→    /// A pending ``receive()`` resolves to `nil` (end of stream); pending
   282→    /// connect/send calls fail with ``CmxNetworkByteTransportError/alreadyClosed``.
   283→    public func close() async {
   284→        close(
   285→            pendingError: CmxNetworkByteTransportError.alreadyClosed,
   286→            resumeReceiveWithError: false
   287→        )
   288→    }

   290→    private func startConnect(
   291→        operationID: UUID,
   292→        continuation: CheckedContinuation<Void, any Error>
   293→    ) {
   294→        guard !consumeCancelledOperation(operationID) else {
   295→            continuation.resume(throwing: CancellationError())
   296→            return
   297→        }
   298→        switch state {
   299→        case .idle:
   300→            connectContinuations[operationID] = continuation
   301→            state = .connecting
   302→            scheduleConnectTimeout()
   303→            connection.stateUpdateHandler = { [weak self] state in
   304→                let event = CmxNetworkConnectionEvent(state)
   305→                guard let self else {
   306→                    return
   307→                }
   308→                Task { await self.handleConnectionEvent(event) }
   309→            }
   310→            if tailscaleBinding != nil {
   311→                connection.pathUpdateHandler = { [weak self] path in
   312→                    guard let self else { return }
   313→                    Task { await self.handleTailscalePathUpdate(path) }
   314→                }
   315→            }
   316→            connection.start(queue: callbackQueue)
   317→        case .connecting:
   318→            connectContinuations[operationID] = continuation
   319→        case .ready:
   320→            continuation.resume()
   321→        case let .failed(error):
   322→            continuation.resume(throwing: error)
   323→        case .closed:
   324→            continuation.resume(throwing: CmxNetworkByteTransportError.alreadyClosed)
   325→        }
   326→    }
   327→
   328→    private func handleConnectionEvent(_ event: CmxNetworkConnectionEvent) async {
   329→        switch event {
   330→        case .ready:
   331→            guard !isTerminal else {
   332→                return
   333→            }
   334→            if tailscaleBinding != nil {
   335→                MobileDebugLog.shared.append(
   336→                    "tailscale.connection.ready path=\(Self.pathSummary(connection.currentPath)) revision=\(tailscalePathRevision)"
   337→                )
   338→            }
   339→            do {
   340→                try await validateTailscaleAuthorizationForCurrentPath()
   341→            } catch {
   342→                MobileDebugLog.shared.append(
   343→                    "tailscale.connection.ready_validation_failed error=\(String(describing: error)) path=\(Self.pathSummary(connection.currentPath)) revision=\(tailscalePathRevision)"
   344→                )
   345→                failTransport(.tailscaleAuthorizationUnavailable)
   346→                return
   347→            }
   348→            cancelConnectTimeout()
   349→            state = .ready
   350→            resumeConnectContinuations()
   351→        case let .waiting(errorDescription, kind):
   352→            // Network.framework parks a dial it intends to retry in `.waiting`
   353→            // instead of `.failed` — including connection-refused and
   354→            // host-unreachable, which for our single-address connect are
   355→            // definitive answers, not transient congestion. Left alone, a
   356→            // dead first route (stale Tailscale IP, a code pointing at a
   357→            // machine with no listener) sits in `.waiting` until the connect
   358→            // timeout and adds the whole timeout to scan→pair latency before
   359→            // the caller's next route is tried. Fail the *initial* connect
   360→            // fast on those definitive kinds; once `ready`, waiting events
   361→            // are transient network churn and stay ignored (the RPC layer's
   362→            // liveness watchdog owns mid-stream recovery).
   363→            guard case .connecting = state, waitingKindFailsConnect(kind) else {
   364→                break
   365→            }
   366→            failTransport(.connectionFailed(errorDescription, kind))
   367→        case let .failed(errorDescription, kind):
   368→            failTransport(.connectionFailed(errorDescription, kind))
   369→        case .cancelled:
   370→            switch state {
   371→            case .closed, .failed:
   372→                break
   373→            case .idle, .connecting, .ready:
   374→                close(
   375→                    pendingError: CmxNetworkByteTransportError.alreadyClosed,
   376→                    resumeReceiveWithError: false
   377→                )
   378→            }
   379→        case .other:
   380→            break
   381→        }
   382→    }
   383→
   384→    private func startReceive(
   385→        operationID: UUID,
   386→        continuation: CheckedContinuation<Data?, any Error>
   387→    ) {
   388→        guard !consumeCancelledOperation(operationID) else {
   389→            continuation.resume(throwing: CancellationError())
   390→            return
   391→        }
   392→        switch state {
   393→        case .ready:
   394→            break
   395→        case let .failed(error):
   396→            continuation.resume(throwing: error)
   397→            return
   398→        case .closed:
   399→            continuation.resume(returning: nil)
   400→            return
   401→        case .idle, .connecting:
   402→            continuation.resume(throwing: CmxNetworkByteTransportError.notConnected)
   403→            return
   404→        }
   405→
   406→        if !receiveBuffer.isEmpty {
   407→            continuation.resume(returning: receiveBuffer.removeFirst())
   408→            return
   409→        }
   410→        guard !remoteDidClose else {
   411→            continuation.resume(returning: nil)
   412→            return
   413→        }
   414→        guard receiveContinuation == nil else {
   415→            continuation.resume(throwing: CmxNetworkByteTransportError.receiveAlreadyInProgress)
   416→            return
   417→        }
   418→
   419→        receiveContinuation = (operationID, continuation)
   420→        if receiveInFlightOperationID == nil {
   421→            issueReceive(operationID: operationID)
   422→        }
   423→    }
   424→
   425→    private func issueReceive(operationID: UUID) {
   426→        receiveInFlightOperationID = operationID
   427→        connection.receive(
   428→            minimumIncompleteLength: 1,
   429→            maximumLength: maximumReceiveLength
   430→        ) { [weak self] data, _, isComplete, error in
   431→            let errorDescription = error.map(\.cmxUserFacingDescription)
   432→            guard let self else {
   433→                return
   434→            }
   435→            Task {
   436→                await self.handleReceive(
   437→                    operationID: operationID,
   438→                    data: data,
   439→                    isComplete: isComplete,
   440→                    errorDescription: errorDescription
   441→                )
   442→            }
   443→        }
   444→    }
   445→
   446→    private func handleReceive(
   447→        operationID: UUID,
   448→        data: Data?,
   449→        isComplete: Bool,
   450→        errorDescription: String?
   451→    ) {
   452→        _ = consumeCancelledOperation(operationID)
   453→        if receiveInFlightOperationID == operationID {
   454→            receiveInFlightOperationID = nil
   455→        }
   456→        guard !isTerminal else {
   457→            return
   458→        }
   459→
   460→        if let errorDescription {
   461→            let error = CmxNetworkByteTransportError.receiveFailed(errorDescription)
   462→            failTransport(error)
   463→            return
   464→        }
   465→
   466→        if let data, !data.isEmpty {
   467→            remoteDidClose = isComplete
   468→            deliverReceivedData(data)
   469→            return
   470→        }
   471→
   472→        if isComplete {
   473→            remoteDidClose = true
   474→            deliverEndOfStream()
   475→            return
   476→        }
   477→
   478→        if let pending = receiveContinuation {
   479→            issueReceive(operationID: pending.id)
   480→        }
   481→    }
   482→
   483→    private func deliverReceivedData(_ data: Data) {
   484→        guard let pending = receiveContinuation else {
   485→            receiveBuffer.append(data)
   486→            return
   487→        }
   488→        receiveContinuation = nil
   489→        pending.continuation.resume(returning: data)
   490→    }
   491→
   492→    private func deliverEndOfStream() {
   493→        guard let pending = receiveContinuation else {
   494→            return
   495→        }
   496→        receiveContinuation = nil
   497→        pending.continuation.resume(returning: nil)
   498→    }

   500→    private func startSend(
   501→        _ data: Data,
   502→        operationID: UUID,
   503→        continuation: CheckedContinuation<Void, any Error>
   504→    ) async {
   505→        guard !consumeCancelledOperation(operationID) else {
   506→            continuation.resume(throwing: CancellationError())
   507→            return
   508→        }
   509→        switch state {
   510→        case .ready:
   511→            break
   512→        case let .failed(error):
   513→            continuation.resume(throwing: error)
   514→            return
   515→        case .closed:
   516→            continuation.resume(throwing: CmxNetworkByteTransportError.alreadyClosed)
   517→            return
   518→        case .idle, .connecting:
   519→            continuation.resume(throwing: CmxNetworkByteTransportError.notConnected)
   520→            return
   521→        }
   522→
   523→        guard sendContinuation == nil else {
   524→            continuation.resume(throwing: CmxNetworkByteTransportError.sendAlreadyInProgress)
   525→            return
   526→        }
   527→
   528→        do {
   529→            try await performAuthorizedWrite(
   530→                authorization: {
   531→                    try await validateTailscaleAuthorizationForCurrentPath()
   532→                },
   533→                beginWrite: {
   534→                    beginSend(
   535→                        data,
   536→                        operationID: operationID,
   537→                        continuation: continuation
   538→                    )
   539→                }
   540→            )
   541→        } catch {
   542→            let transportError = CmxNetworkByteTransportError.tailscaleAuthorizationUnavailable
   543→            continuation.resume(throwing: transportError)
   544→            failTransport(transportError)
   545→        }
   546→    }
   547→
   548→    private func beginSend(
   549→        _ data: Data,
   550→        operationID: UUID,
   551→        continuation: CheckedContinuation<Void, any Error>
   552→    ) {
   553→        sendContinuation = (operationID, continuation)
   554→        connection.send(
   555→            content: data,
   556→            contentContext: .defaultMessage,
   557→            isComplete: false,
   558→            completion: .contentProcessed { [weak self] error in
   559→                let errorDescription = error.map(\.cmxUserFacingDescription)
   560→                guard let self else { return }
   561→                Task {
   562→                    await self.handleSend(
   563→                        operationID: operationID,
   564→                        errorDescription: errorDescription
   565→                    )
   566→                }
   567→            }
   568→        )
   569→    }
   570→
   571→    private func handleSend(operationID: UUID, errorDescription: String?) {
   572→        _ = consumeCancelledOperation(operationID)
   573→        guard let pending = sendContinuation, pending.id == operationID else {
   574→            return
   575→        }
   576→        sendContinuation = nil
   577→
   578→        if let errorDescription {
   579→            let error = CmxNetworkByteTransportError.sendFailed(errorDescription)
   580→            failTransport(error)
   581→            pending.continuation?.resume(throwing: error)
   582→            return
   583→        }
   584→
   585→        pending.continuation?.resume()
   586→    }
   587→
   588→    private func failTransport(_ error: CmxNetworkByteTransportError) {
   589→        guard !isTerminal else {
   590→            return
   591→        }
   592→        cancelConnectTimeout()
   593→        state = .failed(error)
   594→        cancelledOperationIDs.removeAll()
   595→        receiveBuffer.removeAll()
   596→        receiveInFlightOperationID = nil
   597→        connection.stateUpdateHandler = nil
   598→        connection.pathUpdateHandler = nil
   599→        connection.cancel()
   600→        resumeConnectContinuations(throwing: error)
   601→        resumeReceiveContinuation(throwing: error)
   602→        resumeSendContinuation(throwing: error)
   603→    }
   604→
   605→    private func close(pendingError: any Error, resumeReceiveWithError: Bool) {
   606→        guard !isClosed else {
   607→            return
   608→        }
   609→        cancelConnectTimeout()
   610→        state = .closed
   611→        cancelledOperationIDs.removeAll()
   612→        receiveBuffer.removeAll()
   613→        receiveInFlightOperationID = nil
   614→        connection.stateUpdateHandler = nil
   615→        connection.pathUpdateHandler = nil
   616→        connection.cancel()
   617→        resumeConnectContinuations(throwing: pendingError)
   618→        if resumeReceiveWithError {
   619→            resumeReceiveContinuation(throwing: pendingError)
   620→        } else {
   621→            resumeReceiveContinuation(returning: nil)
   622→        }
   623→        resumeSendContinuation(throwing: pendingError)
   624→    }
   625→
   626→    private func cancelConnect(operationID: UUID) {
   627→        if let continuation = connectContinuations.removeValue(forKey: operationID) {
   628→            continuation.resume(throwing: CancellationError())
   629→        } else {
   630→            cancelledOperationIDs.insert(operationID)
   631→        }
   632→    }
   633→
   634→    private func cancelReceive(operationID: UUID) {
   635→        if let pending = receiveContinuation, pending.id == operationID {
   636→            receiveContinuation = nil
   637→            pending.continuation.resume(throwing: CancellationError())
   638→        } else {
   639→            cancelledOperationIDs.insert(operationID)
   640→        }
   641→    }
   642→
   643→    private func cancelSend(operationID: UUID) {
   644→        if let pending = sendContinuation, pending.id == operationID {
   645→            sendContinuation = nil
   646→            cancelledOperationIDs.insert(operationID)
   647→            pending.continuation?.resume(throwing: CancellationError())
   648→        } else {
   649→            cancelledOperationIDs.insert(operationID)
   650→        }
   651→    }
   652→
   653→    private func consumeCancelledOperation(_ operationID: UUID) -> Bool {
   654→        cancelledOperationIDs.remove(operationID) != nil
   655→    }
   656→
   657→    private func scheduleConnectTimeout() {
   658→        cancelConnectTimeout()
   659→        let timer = DispatchSource.makeTimerSource(queue: callbackQueue)
   660→        timer.schedule(
   661→            deadline: .now() + DispatchTimeInterval.milliseconds(
   662→                coveringNanoseconds: connectTimeoutNanoseconds
   663→            )
   664→        )
   665→        timer.setEventHandler { [weak self] in
   666→            guard let self else {
   667→                return
   668→            }
   669→            Task { await self.handleConnectTimeout() }
   670→        }
   671→        connectTimeoutTimer = timer
   672→        timer.resume()
   673→    }
   674→
   675→    private func cancelConnectTimeout() {
   676→        connectTimeoutTimer?.setEventHandler {}
   677→        connectTimeoutTimer?.cancel()
   678→        connectTimeoutTimer = nil
   679→    }
   680→
   681→    private func handleConnectTimeout() {
   682→        guard case .connecting = state else {
   683→            return
   684→        }
   685→        failTransport(.connectionTimedOut)
   686→    }

   688→    private func handleTailscalePathUpdate(_ path: NWPath) async {
   689→        guard tailscaleBinding != nil, !isTerminal else { return }
   690→        tailscalePathRevision = tailscalePathRevision == .max ? 1 : tailscalePathRevision + 1
   691→        MobileDebugLog.shared.append(
   692→            "tailscale.connection.path_update revision=\(tailscalePathRevision) path=\(Self.pathSummary(path))"
   693→        )
   694→        do {
   695→            // This callback can fire before the connection binds its local
   696→            // endpoint, so only route-level facts exist here; the endpoint
   697→            // facts are asserted at ready and at every write boundary.
   698→            try await validateTailscaleAuthorization(path: path, phase: .pathUpdate)
   699→        } catch {
   700→            MobileDebugLog.shared.append(
   701→                "tailscale.connection.path_validation_failed error=\(String(describing: error)) revision=\(tailscalePathRevision) path=\(Self.pathSummary(path))"
   702→            )
   703→            tailscaleAuthorizationInvalidated = true
   704→            failTransport(.tailscaleAuthorizationUnavailable)
   705→        }
   706→    }
   707→
   708→    private func validateTailscaleAuthorizationForCurrentPath() async throws {
   709→        guard tailscaleBinding != nil else { return }
   710→        guard let path = connection.currentPath else {
   711→            throw CmxNetworkByteTransportError.tailscaleAuthorizationUnavailable
   712→        }
   713→        let revision = tailscalePathRevision
   714→        try await validateTailscaleAuthorization(path: path, phase: .established)
   715→        // The authority call yields this actor. Reject any connection-path
   716→        // update that interleaved before the synchronous send boundary.
   717→        guard revision == tailscalePathRevision else {
   718→            throw CmxNetworkByteTransportError.tailscaleAuthorizationUnavailable
   719→        }
   720→    }
   721→
   722→    private func validateTailscaleAuthorization(
   723→        path: NWPath,
   724→        phase: CmxTailscaleRouteValidationPhase
   725→    ) async throws {
   726→        guard let binding = tailscaleBinding else { return }
   727→        MobileDebugLog.shared.append(
   728→            "tailscale.authorization.validate_begin phase=\(phase) path=\(Self.pathSummary(path)) revision=\(tailscalePathRevision)"
   729→        )
   730→        guard !tailscaleAuthorizationInvalidated,
   731→              binding.request == binding.preparedRoute.proof.request,
   732→              connection.parameters.requiredInterface == binding.preparedRoute.requiredInterface else {
   733→            MobileDebugLog.shared.append(
   734→                "tailscale.authorization.validate_precondition_failed invalidated=\(tailscaleAuthorizationInvalidated) request_matches=\(binding.request == binding.preparedRoute.proof.request) interface_matches=\(connection.parameters.requiredInterface == binding.preparedRoute.requiredInterface)"
   735→            )
   736→            throw CmxNetworkByteTransportError.tailscaleAuthorizationUnavailable
   737→        }
   738→        do {
   739→            try await binding.authority.validate(
   740→                proof: binding.preparedRoute.proof,
   741→                connectionPath: path,
   742→                phase: phase
   743→            )
   744→            MobileDebugLog.shared.append("tailscale.authorization.validate_success phase=\(phase)")
   745→        } catch {
   746→            MobileDebugLog.shared.append(
   747→                "tailscale.authorization.validate_failed underlying=\(String(describing: error)) phase=\(phase) path=\(Self.pathSummary(path))"
   748→            )
   749→            throw CmxNetworkByteTransportError.tailscaleAuthorizationUnavailable
   750→        }
   751→    }
   752→
   753→    private static func pathSummary(_ path: NWPath?) -> String {
   754→        guard let path else { return "nil" }
   755→        let interfaces = path.availableInterfaces
   756→            .map { "\($0.name):\($0.index)" }
   757→            .sorted()
   758→            .joined(separator: ",")
   759→        return "status=\(path.status) interfaces=\(interfaces) local=\(path.localEndpoint != nil) remote=\(path.remoteEndpoint != nil)"
   760→    }

   762→    /// The single legacy bearer-write boundary. Authorization completes before
   763→    /// Network.framework receives the send request.
   764→    func performAuthorizedWrite(
   765→        authorization: () async throws -> Void,
   766→        beginWrite: () -> Void
   767→    ) async rethrows {
   768→        try await authorization()
   769→        beginWrite()

   772→    private var isTerminal: Bool {
   773→        switch state {
   774→        case .failed, .closed:
   775→            return true
   776→        case .idle, .connecting, .ready:
   777→            return false
   778→        }
   779→    }

   781→    private var isClosed: Bool {
   782→        if case .closed = state {
   783→            return true
   784→        }
   785→        return false

   788→    private func resumeConnectContinuations(throwing error: (any Error)? = nil) {
   789→        let continuations = connectContinuations.values
   790→        connectContinuations.removeAll()
   791→        for continuation in continuations {
   792→            if let error {
   793→                continuation.resume(throwing: error)
   794→            } else {
   795→                continuation.resume()
   796→            }
   797→        }
   798→    }
   799→
   800→    private func resumeReceiveContinuation(
   801→        returning data: Data? = nil,
   802→        throwing error: (any Error)? = nil
   803→    ) {
   804→        guard let pending = receiveContinuation else {
   805→            return
   806→        }
   807→        receiveContinuation = nil
   808→        if let error {
   809→            pending.continuation.resume(throwing: error)
   810→        } else {
   811→            pending.continuation.resume(returning: data)
   812→        }
   813→    }

     4→/// Decodes a scanned or pasted `cmux-ios://` pairing/attach URL into a
     5→/// validated ``CmxAttachTicket``.
     6→public struct CmxAttachTicketInput {
     7→    private init() {}
     8→
     9→    /// Decode and validate a `cmux-ios://pair` or `cmux-ios://attach` URL.
    10→    ///
    11→    /// Attach tickets are validated structurally only; a scanned QR keeps
    12→    /// working however long it sat on the Mac's screen (the host authorizes
    13→    /// by Stack account, not ticket age). Only the ancient `cmux-ios://pair`
    14→    /// grammar still enforces its own expiry.
    15→    /// - Parameter rawValue: The scanned/pasted URL string.
    16→    /// - Returns: A validated attach ticket.
    17→    /// - Throws: `MobileSyncPairingPayloadError.invalidURL` or any ticket
    18→    ///   validation error if the input is malformed, or
    19→    ///   `MobileSyncPairingPayloadError.loopbackRouteRejected` for a v2
    20→    ///   pairing code whose routes point at the phone itself.
    21→    public static func decode(_ rawValue: String) throws -> CmxAttachTicket {
    22→        guard let url = URL(string: rawValue) else {
    23→            throw MobileSyncPairingPayloadError.invalidURL
    24→        }
    25→        // Accept any channel's pairing scheme (cmux-ios for release builds,
    26→        // cmux-ios-dev for development); cross-channel pairing still works when
    27→        // the user scans from inside the app. The emitter picks the matching
    28→        // scheme so the *system camera* routes each channel's QR to its build.
    29→        if CmxPairingURLScheme(rawValue: url.scheme) != nil, url.host == "pair" {
    30→            return try ticket(from: MobileSyncPairingPayload.decodeURL(url))
    31→        }
    32→        guard CmxPairingURLScheme(rawValue: url.scheme) != nil,
    33→              url.host == "attach",
    34→              let components = URLComponents(url: url, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false) else {
    35→            throw MobileSyncPairingPayloadError.invalidURL
    36→        }
    37→        // A QR minted by a newer cmux whose grammar version this build does not
    38→        // understand. Distinguished from a malformed code so the user is told
    39→        // to update the app instead of seeing the generic "not valid" copy (the
    40→        // real field report: beta 1.0.2 predated the v2 QR a newer Mac emitted).
    41→        if let version = CmxPairingQRCode.attachURLVersion(components),
    42→           version > CmxPairingQRCode.version {
    43→            throw MobileSyncPairingPayloadError.unrecognizedURLVersion(version)
    44→        }
    45→        // The plain pairing grammars: v2 carries bare Tailscale routes and v3
    46→        // carries one Iroh EndpointID. v1 carries a base64 JSON payload.
    47→        if CmxPairingQRCode().isPairingCodeURL(components) {
    48→            return try CmxPairingQRCode().decode(components)
    49→        }

    51→              let data = base64URLDecode(encodedPayload) else {
    52→            throw MobileSyncPairingPayloadError.invalidURL

    55→        // short-key form newer Macs put in the pairing QR (top-level "v"),
    56→        // and the legacy full-key Codable form (top-level "version") that

   210→        precondition(maximumDecodedFrameCount > 0)

   212→        frames.reserveCapacity(min(maximumDecodedFrameCount, 16))
   213→        var consumedByteCount = 0

   215→            if consumedByteCount > 0 {

   217→                    buffer.startIndex..<buffer.index(

   219→                        offsetBy: consumedByteCount

   238→            guard payloadLength <= maximumFrameByteCount else {

     3→/// Codes ``CmxAttachTicket`` to and from the compact wire form used by the
     4→/// pairing QR payload.
     5→///
     6→/// The pairing QR encodes `cmux-ios://attach?v=1&payload=<base64url(JSON)>`.
     7→/// The legacy JSON spelled out full camelCase keys plus a vestigial
     8→/// `auth_token`, which pushed the QR into a denser version than necessary.
     9→/// The compact grammar keeps the same envelope but encodes only what pairing
    10→/// actually consumes: short keys, no empty optional fields, no auth token, no
    11→/// display name (read post-handshake from `mobile.host.status`), and no
    12→/// expiry. It does keep non-secret pairing context: the Mac account email,
    13→/// shared pairing compatibility level, and app version/build, so the phone can
    14→/// fail fast on an account mismatch and warn before continuing across
    15→/// compatibility skew. A pairing QR never expires;
    16→/// the owner's Stack access token is the
    17→/// host's sole authorization gate (`MobileHostService.authorizationError(for:)`),
    18→/// so ticket age authorizes nothing.
    19→///
    20→/// Compatibility:
    21→/// - New decoders accept both grammars: ``CmxAttachTicketInput`` routes a
    22→///   payload whose top-level object carries `"v"` here and everything else
    23→///   (legacy `"version"` payloads) through the original `Codable` path.
    24→/// - Payloads from the first compact revision still decode: their extra `e`
    25→///   (expiry) and `n` (display name) keys are ignored, their explicit route
    26→///   `i` ids and endpoint `t` types are honored.
    27→/// - Old decoders reject the compact grammar loudly (a `DecodingError` from
    28→///   the missing `"version"` key), so an outdated phone scanning a new QR
    29→///   shows a pairing error instead of silently misreading the ticket.
    30→///
    31→/// Key map (ticket): `v` version, `w` workspaceID (omitted when empty),
    32→/// `t` terminalID, `d` macDeviceID, `u` Mac account email, `pc` pairing
    33→/// compatibility version, `av` app version, `ab` app build, `r` routes.
    34→/// Key map (route): `i` id (omitted when the decoder can resynthesize it:
    35→/// `kind` for the first route of a kind, `kind_N` for the Nth), `k` kind raw
    36→/// value, `p` priority (omitted when 0), `e` endpoint.
    37→/// Key map (endpoint): the type is implied by the keys present (accepted
    38→/// explicitly under `t` for first-revision payloads): `h` host + `p` port, or
    39→/// `i` peer id, or `u` url. New pairing payloads carry no Iroh path hints:
    40→/// managed relays are app configuration, online discovery is authenticated,
    41→/// and offline pairing resolves the scanned EndpointID locally. Decoding still
    42→/// accepts the first compact revision's `ph`, `rh`, `da`, and `ru` fields.
    43→public struct CmxAttachTicketCompactCoder: Sendable {
    44→    /// Creates a coder. The coder is stateless; instances are interchangeable.
    45→    public init() {}
    46→
    47→    /// Encode a ticket into the compact JSON grammar.
    48→    ///
    49→    /// Any `authToken`, `macDisplayName`, and `expiresAt` on the ticket are
    50→    /// intentionally not encoded: the token never authorizes anything on the
    51→    /// host (Stack auth is the sole gate), the name is read post-handshake
    52→    /// from `mobile.host.status`, and a pairing QR never expires. Callers must
    53→    /// explicitly select identity-only disclosure or the temporary released-
    54→    /// client compatibility mode.
    55→    public func encode(
    56→        _ ticket: CmxAttachTicket,
    57→        routeDisclosureMode: CmxPairingRouteDisclosureMode
    58→    ) throws -> Data {
    59→        let encoder = JSONEncoder()
    60→        encoder.outputFormatting = [.sortedKeys, .withoutEscapingSlashes]
    61→        return try encoder.encode(CompactAttachTicket(
    62→            ticket,
    63→            routeDisclosureMode: routeDisclosureMode
    64→        ))
    65→    }
    66→
    67→    /// Decode a compact JSON payload into a validated ``CmxAttachTicket``.
    68→    public func decode(_ data: Data) throws -> CmxAttachTicket {
    69→        try JSONDecoder().decode(CompactAttachTicket.self, from: data).ticket()
    70→    }
    71→
    72→    /// Whether a decoded `payload` blob speaks the compact grammar.
    73→    ///
    74→    /// Compact payloads carry the version under `"v"`; legacy payloads carry
    75→    /// it under `"version"`. Non-JSON input returns `false` so the caller
    76→    /// falls through to the legacy decoder, which throws a proper error.
    77→    public func isCompactPayload(_ data: Data) -> Bool {
    78→        guard let object = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any] else {
    79→            return false
    80→        }
    81→        return object["v"] != nil
    82→    }
    83→}
    84→
